To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

households that adopted only solar hot water and/or photovoltaic systems had a long term reduction in their electricity consumption, and that households that adopted a combination of renewable energy and energy efficient measures reduced their electricity consumption more than those households that adopted only renewable energy measures.
the adoption of solar photovoltaic systems and solar hot water systems reduced household electricity consumption in the long term, while the adoption of energy efficiency alone did not.

households who adopt renewable energy technologies and energy efficiency measures have lower energy usage in the long term, but that the reduction is greater for those who adopt both technologies and energy efficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how to increase the uptake and use of energy efficiency measures in households.
understanding the role of the household in the uptake of energy efficiency and renewable energy technologies, and the role of the Solar City programme in facilitating this uptake.
the relationship between energy efficiency measures, renewable energy technologies and the reduction in electricity usage, and how these relate to household behaviour.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
households who adopt energy efficiency measures do not have a significant long term reduction in electricity usage, but households that adopt renewable energy technology do.
, while there is evidence of a rebound effect, there is also evidence that the adoption of energy efficiency and renewable energy technology can lead to significant energy reduction.
households that participated in the Solar City programme reduced their electricity usage by an average of 15% over the 5-year study period.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
households that adopt renewable energy technologies and a number of energy efficiency technologies will have the greatest reduction in energy use.
the Solar Cities programme had a positive influence on the uptake of energy efficiency measures, but that the impact on energy usage was not as large as anticipated.

households that adopt renewable energy technology reduce their electricity usage by more than those that adopt only energy efficiency measures, but that both are important in reducing electricity consumption.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of renewable energy and energy efficient measures can lead to a long-term reduction in household electricity usage.
the adoption of energy efficiency and renewable energy measures is a good first step to reducing household electricity use.
the Solar City Alice Springs program has been successful in reducing household electricity usage.
